devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two words in Hebrew, and they rest on something stated at the very beginning:
human beings are made in God's image (Gen 1:27). To destroy a person is to
attack something that bears God's likeness.

That is the reasoning God Himself gives after the flood: "for in the image of God
has God made mankind" (Gen 9:6). Human life is not valuable because it is useful,
productive, wanted, or convenient. It is valuable because of whose image it
carries.

Then Jesus takes this command somewhere uncomfortable. "Anyone who is angry with
a brother or sister will be subject to judgment" (Matt 5:22). He traces murder
back to its root. Most of us will never take a life. Most of us have wished
someone diminished, humiliated, or gone.

John says it plainly: "Anyone who hates a brother or sister is a murderer"
(1 John 3:15).

That is not a comfortable teaching, and it is not meant to be. It closes the door
on the idea that we are basically fine because our hands are clean.

The command protects human life. Christ's exposition protects the human heart.
And both drive us to the only place that helps: mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there anyone you have written off in your heart?
2. Do you treat every person as an image-bearer, including the inconvenient
   ones?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, search my heart for contempt and anger I have excused. Teach me to see
every person as made in Your image. Amen.
